dimensions.label: Cheapest way to start
dimensions.a: $97 a month (Starter); no free plan; a 14-day trial from the pricing page, or 30 days through HighLevel's Bootcamp page
dimensions.b: $0 on the free tools (2 users, 1,000 contacts); $20 a seat a month on Starter

dimensions.label: How texting is sold
dimensions.a: Included on every plan, billed per segment plus a carrier fee as you send
dimensions.b: Not sold on the free tools or Starter; a $75-a-month add-on on Professional or Enterprise only, U.S. numbers only

dimensions.label: Onboarding fee
dimensions.b: $3,000 one-time on Professional; $7,000 one-time on Enterprise, charged automatically on purchase

dimensions.label: Minimum contract
dimensions.a: Month-to-month on every plan; annual billing is optional
dimensions.b: Starter is month-to-month; Professional requires a 12-month commitment; Enterprise is annual only

dimensions.label: Users and contacts
dimensions.a: Unlimited users and unlimited contacts on every plan, including Starter
dimensions.b: Free tools cap at 2 users and 1,000 contacts; paid seats cost $20-$75 each and contacts bill in tiers that step up as the list grows

dimensions.label: Multi-client structure for agencies
dimensions.a: Built-in sub-accounts: 3 on Starter, unlimited on Unlimited and Agency Pro
dimensions.b: No sub-account system; each client would need its own separate subscription

dimensions.label: Website and funnel builder
dimensions.a: Website, funnel and landing-page builder included on every plan
dimensions.b: Landing pages included; no funnel builder

dimensions.label: One record across marketing, sales and service
dimensions.a: CRM and pipelines built in, but no separate sales or service hub
dimensions.b: Marketing, sales, service and content hubs all read and write the same Smart CRM record

dimensions.label: Pricing transparency
dimensions.a: Plan and add-on prices are public, but usage rates sit across many help-center articles that do not always agree with each other
dimensions.b: List prices, contact tiers, add-ons and limits published in one Product & Services Catalog, plus a public price calculator

dimensions.label: AI features
dimensions.a: Metered per token or per minute, or a flat $50 or $97 per-location AI Employee add-on
dimensions.b: HubSpot Credits included per tier; extra credits cost $0.01 each

verdicts.why: GoHighLevel's sub-accounts let an agency run each client as its own workspace under one subscription, while HubSpot has no comparable sub-account system, so managing several clients on HubSpot would mean a separate subscription for each one.

GoHighLevel's courses feature and HubSpot's content tools are both add-ons bolted onto a CRM, not a dedicated course platform, so a course creator is better served by a tool built around cohorts, lessons and student progress.
Neither tool is an ecommerce platform; a Shopify store needs a shopping cart, product catalog and checkout, not a CRM or a marketing hub.

GoHighLevel bundles a CRM, booking calendar, review requests and SMS follow-up that a clinic, contractor or salon runs every day in one flat-plus-usage bill, while HubSpot is built as marketing-and-sales software rather than a front-desk system for appointments and reviews.

A freelancer with a short contact list can run HubSpot's free tools at $0 with no usage wallet to fund, while GoHighLevel's cheapest plan starts at $97 a month for sub-account and phone-system features a solo operator will not use.

HubSpot's Marketing Hub fits a SaaS startup building a sales-and-marketing motion from scratch, with lead scoring and workflows suited to a product-led sales cycle that GoHighLevel's agency-first, sub-account design is not built around.
